Subject: Post-call: Multilingual model suitability + pilot proposal (EU/APAC focus)

Hi Sara, Tom —

Thanks again for a productive discussion today. Quick recap + recommended next steps based on the call: 

Quick recap
- Use case: customer support triage + short answer generation for RetailCorp's EU storefronts (FR/DE/ES) and APAC pilot (JA/KO/VI).
- Constraints: strict PII redaction for EU, localized tone requirements per market, sub-100ms avg token latency target for UI flow, budget sensitivity for pilot.

Initial model recommendations (for evaluation)
- rw-mt-7b-q4f (compact multilingual, best cost/latency balance for JA/KO/VI)
- rw-instruct-13b-8bit (higher-quality for FR/DE/ES; keep as fallback for long-form replies)
- rw-mini-3b-quant (cheap, lower-latency candidate for classification/triage tasks)

Artifacts attached / links
- prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attached) — first-pass prompts per locale and 50-shot example set
- eu-apac-benchmarks-quickview.csv (attached) — lightweight metric table from our sandbox runs
- eval plan drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3Example

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood runs a focused pilot evaluation across the 6 locales using the attached prompt set (2 weeks). Deliverables: per-locale quality matrix, perplexity + ROUGE quick checks, latency P50/P95.
2) RetailCorp provides 1-2 anonymized exemplar threads per locale for fine-grained prompts (GDPR-safe).
3) Joint review call to pick a pilot model and define pilot SLAs and success criteria.

Would you be able to:
- Share the exemplar threads (anonymized) by Feb 15?
- Confirm whether we should include your localized tone guide for FR/DE/ES in the prompt set?

I'll draft a brief eval plan and cost estimate once we have the exemplar data.

Best,

- Include a targeted stress test for FR/DE peak hour slices.

Sara —

Appreciate the callouts. I’ve attached a succinct eval plan PDF and included the tokenization notes below to address the immediate legal/security questions. I’ll loop in our security contact if we need a formal diagram.

Quick tokenization notes (rw-mt-7b-q4f / rw-instruct-13b-8bit)
- Both models use a byte-level tokenizer with language-aware merges; uncommon diacritics are preserved as composed characters, not stripped. For Vietnamese we recommend preserving full Unicode normalization NFC.
- Japanese: tokenizer treats common honorific sequences as single tokens for a base vocabulary; we recommend prompt examples that keep honorifics contiguous (e.g., "san", "sama" attached to names).
- If you want, we can provide a small tokenization demo script for your legal/security review.

Attached: redwood-eval-plan.pdf (includes privacy addendum language and 30-day retention clause). Pilot scope highlights:
- Duration: 2 weeks of runs + 3-day stress window
- Locales: FR, DE, ES, JA, KO, VI
- Metrics: locale-specific F1 for intent classification, mean opinion score (MOS) blind eval sample per locale (n=200), latency P50/P95, token cost estimate
- Deliverables: per-locale scorecard, redlines for prompts, and recommended model mapping per route (triage vs. answer generation).

Next steps I propose:
1) Sara/Tom: confirm anonymized exemplar timelines (Feb 15 ideal).
2) Nikhil/Neha: Redwood to spin the pilot run and share a cost estimate by Feb 14.
3) Joint kickoff call week of Feb 22 to review pilot plan and success criteria.

Neha — assigning you the action item to prepare the quick tokenization demo and an initial cost run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
